title: Chapter 65: Soft 3
content:
Chapter 65

Soft 3

Lan Wangji closed the distance and handed him the jars of Emperor’s Smile. Cradling the liquor against his chest, Wei Wuxian turned and ducked inside the cottage. Watching his retreating back, Lan Wangji let out a nearly imperceptible shake of his head, though his pale eyes softened with quiet warmth.

Beside him, Lan Xichen caught the look. "You brought those from your own quarters?"

Lan Wangji nodded.

Lan Xichen hesitated. "You... shouldn't drink. Be careful not to let history repeat itself."

His gaze drifted down toward the collar of Lan Wangji’s inner robes. Lan Wangji lowered his eyes, glancing at the fabric covering his own chest. "It won't happen again."

Lan Xichen managed a faint, strained smile, answering only with a heavy sigh.

Once his brother left, Lan Wangji stepped into the cottage and pulled the door shut behind him. Across the room, Wei Wuxian was busy peeling the wax seals off the jars, his mind still turning over the tragic legacies of Lan An and Qingheng-jun. The Gusu Lan Clan really is a total paradox, he mused. Founded by a monk and rigid to a fault, yet scratch the surface and they’re all... hopeless romantics.

Following that thought, his eyes drifted naturally toward the living heir of that bloodline.

Lan Wangji was sitting upright at the low desk, head bowed over an open book. A solitary paper lantern flickered in the corner, its warm glow washing over features carved like mutton-fat jade. Even that trademark icy detachment and those pale, glassy eyes looked softened by the amber light—strikingly handsome, almost unreal. Wei Wuxian caught himself staring, completely mesmerized, his feet moving on pure instinct until he found himself leaning over the table.

Lan Wangji’s lashes lifted. "Something the matter?"

Wei Wuxian snapped out of his daze in a flash. "Nothing. Just admiring your bookmark."

The bookmark was a single pressed blossom—a pale, dried flower preserved with astonishing care. The petals had retained their delicate blush, the intricate veins frozen as if still drawing sap, slipping between the pages while exhaling a faint, clean perfume. Wei Wuxian pinched the stem, lifting it into the light. "A peony?"

"Mm."

Wei Wuxian turned it over once or twice, then handed it back. "Your brother looked pretty shaken up."

Carefully setting the dried peony back between the leaves, Lan Wangji closed the book. "Once we have definitive proof, he will not look the other way."

"Naturally. He's your brother, after all."

No matter how close Lan Xichen and Jin Guangyao were, a Lan was still a Lan. The man had an iron spine when it came to his principles.

Wei Wuxian popped the clay seal off one of the jars, his mind wandering again. Last time Lan Zhan got plastered, he gave me a straight answer: he never snuck sips of the stash in his room. So why hoard Emperor’s Smile in the first place? It’s not like he kept it around just for me... No, that’s way too vain. Then again, should I apologize about the forehead ribbon? I’ve messed with it so many times now. What if he dies of mortification and kicks me to the curb? But I've been running wild for weeks and he hasn't lost his temper once; his patience really has leveled up. Maybe he won't mind if I push my luck a little more. Actually, I shouldn't bring it up at all. Better to play dumb and pretend I haven't the faintest clue what the ribbon means. That way, next time I yank it, I can just flash an innocent grin and say, 'Sorry, had no idea!' Ignorance is bliss...

Giddy with his own genius, a smirk broke across his face.

Lan Wangji caught the look. "What is it?"

Wei Wuxian smoothed his expression instantly. "Nothing! Just in a good mood."

Distracted, he grabbed the open jar, tipped his head back, and took a deep swig—only to spray a mouthful of liquid straight across the floorboards.

Lan Wangji set his book down on the desk. "Now what?"

Wei Wuxian waved a frantic hand, coughing. "Nothing! Totally fine, totally fine!"

Protesting loudly that nothing was wrong, he shoved the offending jar to the side and hastily grabbed the second one, his face an absolute picture of cursed defeat.

During his last visit, he’d chugged a few jars and topped it off with well water, scheming to prank Lan Wangji whenever the man decided to take a sip. Of all the rotten luck in the world, out of the two jars Lan Wangji had fetched tonight, he’d grabbed the exact one filled with plain tap water—and Wei Wuxian had walked right into his own trap.

Ever since his resurrection, every single petty prank he’d aimed at Lan Wangji had boomeranged straight back into his own face. It was completely infuriating!

Wei Wuxian had no idea when he’d finally crashed, drifting through a heavy, dreamless sleep until the small hours of the morning.

A sudden jolt of instinct snapped him awake. He scrambled upright to find Lan Wangji fully dressed, guqin and spiritual sword strapped across his back. Lan Wangji drew his hand away from Wei Wuxian's shoulder, his gaze locked onto an object resting in his palm.

"An uninvited guest," Lan Wangji said quietly.

Wei Wuxian squinted through the dim light. It was the Lan Clan’s jade entry token. He remembered Lan Wangji’s token was of the highest clearance, designed to hum with a warning resonance whenever an outsider breached the protective perimeter of the Cloud Recesses.

Yet no one had dared trespass across their wards in over a decade. Wei Wuxian rolled out of bed, only to notice his outer robe had been peeled off while he slept. Fumbling with the sash as he slipped it back on, he whispered, "Who is it?"

Lan Wangji gave a slight shake of his head, gesturing for him to follow. Slipping through the shadows, they navigated a path screened by dense bamboo until they arrived outside a quiet pavilion, a warm lantern glowing behind the paper lattice.

Wei Wuxian caught sight of the wooden plaque hung above the courtyard. "The Hanshi?"

Sure enough, Lan Xichen was seated inside with immaculate posture. He didn't blink an eye as the two slipped over the threshold, trading a quiet, loaded look with his brother before Lan Wangji steered Wei Wuxian behind a standing screen.

A few moments later, the bamboo blinds at the entrance were lifted. Light, measured footsteps brushed across the floorboards, settling opposite Lan Xichen.

A crisp chime of jade striking wood broke the silence—an object was slid across the low table.

Lan Xichen was the first to speak. "What is the meaning of this?"

A smooth, familiar voice answered: "Returning it to Er-ge."

Jin Guangyao.

Lan Xichen said, "I gave that to you as a gift."

"This jade token granted me passage for years without fail," Jin Guangyao replied gently. "Now that its clearance has been revoked, it is only proper to return it to its true owner."

Wei Wuxian pieced it together instantly. Given the deep brotherhood between Ze-wu-jun and Lianfang-zun, Lan Xichen had granted Jin Guangyao an unrestricted pass to enter the Cloud Recesses at will. But over the past few days, Lan Xichen must have altered the mountain's boundary arrays or quietly stripped Jin Guangyao’s token of its spiritual authority. When Jin Guangyao arrived tonight, he’d found the gates barred, leaving him no choice but to formally surrender the token.

Much like his younger brother, Lan Xichen had never mastered the art of deceitful pleasantries. Met with Jin Guangyao’s calculated humility, he simply held his tongue.

After a long pause, he asked, "Why have you come?"

"We still have no word on Hanguang-jun or the Yiling Laozu," Jin Guangyao explained smoothly. "I blocked the other clans from searching the Cloud Recesses, but suspicions are mounting, and several clan leaders have voiced strong objections. Whenever it is convenient for you, Er-ge, perhaps leave the outer gates open for an hour so I can lead a cursory patrol and satisfy their curiosity."

Wei Wuxian had assumed the man was here to demand a search warrant. Hearing him actively running interference instead—seemingly entirely uninterested in cornering the Yiling Laozu—left him genuinely caught off guard.

Beyond the screen, Jin Guangyao’s voice softened. "Er-ge, what troubles you?"

"Nothing," Lan Xichen murmured.

"If you are anxious on Wangji’s account, there is no need," Jin Guangyao assured him warmly. "Hanguang-jun’s righteousness and moral standing have been witnessed by the entire cultivation world for decades. Everyone understands he was merely deceived by a villain. Besides, he hasn't committed any irreversible transgressions. Once the dust settles, a simple clarification will suffice. I will not give anyone the opportunity to slander him."

Lan Xichen’s tone remained flat. "Once the dust settles? When?"

"After the Burial Mounds have been cleansed."

Wei Wuxian stiffened.

Lan Xichen echoed, "The Burial Mounds?"

"Ever since the clash at Koi Tower, bizarre anomalies have erupted across Moling, Lanling, and Yunmeng," Jin Guangyao reported. "Graveyards have been desecrated, and corpses have vanished into thin air. Scouts report that a massive horde of the undead is converging toward Yiling. It appears they are gathering at the Burial Mounds."

Lan Xichen frowned. "What could be the purpose of this?"

"Unclear," Jin Guangyao said. "The current consensus is that Wei Wuxian has activated a dark ritual array, or perhaps unleashed the Yin Tiger Tally once more."

"He was run through by Jin Ling’s sword on Koi Tower," Lan Xichen pointed out. "Could he truly muster the spiritual power to orchestrate such an upheaval?"

Jin Guangyao sighed softly. "Er-ge, back when Wei Wuxian defected from the Yunmeng Jiang Clan and fought Sect Leader Jiang, his injuries were catastrophic—yet he returned to summon storms and command legions of the dead without skipping a beat. For the Yiling Laozu, what is impossible?"

Behind the screen, Wei Wuxian rubbed his nose. You flatter me, really...

Jin Guangyao pressed, "A second siege of the Burial Mounds is likely inevitable. I have already summoned the prominent sects to Koi Tower to coordinate our strategy. Er-ge, will you join us?"

After a suffocating beat of silence, Lan Xichen spoke: "I will. Wait for me in the Yashi; I will depart with you shortly."

The moment Jin Guangyao’s steps faded down the corridor, Lan Xichen rounded the standing screen. Meeting Lan Wangji’s gaze, he said quietly, "I will head to Koi Tower. The two of you will make for the Burial Mounds. We divide our efforts."

Lan Wangji dipped his chin. "Understood."

"If he truly harbors treachery," Lan Xichen added, his voice hardening, "I will not protect him."

"I know."

The two descended the mountain via a secluded back path. As they walked, a soft rustle brushed through the tall grass flanking the stone trail, and the greenery parted to reveal a fluffy white puffball of a head crowned by long ears.

The rabbit’s pink nose twitched. Catching sight of Lan Wangji, its droopy ears snapped straight up, kicking its back legs to launch itself straight toward his boots.

They stepped into a clearing of emerald grass where Little Apple was lounging beside a wide tree trunk, completely surrounded by dozens of plump, snowy rabbits. Most were curled up fast asleep, though a few were still snuffling idly in the clover. Wei Wuxian strolled over and gave the donkey’s snout a rough scritch. Little Apple snorted violently, jolting awake; just as he parted his jaw to bray an ear-splitting complaint, the cluster of rabbits startled as well. Long ears twitching, the entire fluffle bounded toward Lan Wangji, swarming around his pristine white boots like rolling clouds, darting in giddy circles for reasons known only to them.

Wei Wuxian caught Little Apple’s reins, dragging the stubborn beast along with playful threats. Meanwhile, the rabbits stood up on their hind legs like tiny humans, forepaws clinging desperately to Lan Wangji’s robes, trying their best to climb.

Lan Wangji remained an unmoving pillar. As they walked, the rabbits stumbled along after the white boots, refusing to disperse no matter how much Wei Wuxian shooed them. Lan Wangji finally bent down, scooping one up into the crook of his arm. His face was as unreadable as ever, but his hands were remarkably gentle as his long fingers stroked the underside of the bunny's chin. The creature twitched its ears, tilting its head into the touch, ruby-red eyes narrowing into happy little slits.

Wei Wuxian reached out to pet it, but the rabbit instantly jerked its nose away.

"Look at that attitude," Wei Wuxian chuckled. "Snubbing me to cling to you—definitely takes after its master."

Lan Wangji looked at him, then gently transferred the warm ball of fluff into Wei Wuxian’s arms. Wei Wuxian grinned, cradling the squirming bundle as it kicked and thrashed against his chest.

Wei Wuxian gave its ear a teasing tug. "Don't like me? Can't stand me? Try to run then! No matter how much you kick, you're not getting away, so you might as well learn to love me."

He fussed over the bunny, thoroughly ruffling its pristine fur until they reached the outer boundary of the Cloud Recesses, finally setting the rumpled little thing down in the grass. Unable to cross the ward line, the rabbits drooped their ears in collective sorrow, perching by the path to watch their master vanish down the trail.

Wei Wuxian glanced back over his shoulder. "They really hate seeing you go, Hanguang-jun. Who would've thought you were such a hit with the critters? You must dote on them something fierce when you're raising them. I could never pull that off."

Lan Wangji looked over. "You couldn't?"

"Nope!" Wei Wuxian declared, puffed up with shameless pride. "Birds in the sky, beasts on the ground, fish in the river—the second they spot me coming, they haul ass in the opposite direction."

Lan Wangji gave a slow, deliberate shake of his head—his silent verdict crystal clear: They run because you terrorize them first.
